questions.q: Define speed and distinguish between uniform and non-uniform motion.

answer.text: Speed is the distance travelled by an object in a unit of time. It is found by dividing the distance travelled by the time taken, and its SI unit is the metre per second, though everyday speeds are often given in kilometres per hour.
When an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, its speed does not change, and its motion is said to be uniform. On a distance–time graph, uniform motion appears as a straight line.
When an object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, its speed keeps changing, and its motion is non-uniform, shown as a curved line on the graph.

answer: A speedometer shows a vehicle's speed and an odometer the distance travelled.

questions.q: What is a simple pendulum? Explain the terms oscillation and time period.
answer: A simple pendulum is a small metal ball, called the bob, hung by a thread from a fixed support so that it can swing freely.

answer.text: When the bob is released, it swings to and fro. One complete to-and-fro movement of the bob is called one oscillation.
The time taken to complete one oscillation is called the time period of the pendulum. For a given pendulum this time period is constant, which is why pendulums were used to measure time.
Galileo noticed this steady rhythm, which led to the invention of pendulum clocks. The time period depends on the length of the pendulum, not on the mass of the bob.
